emma: Quick update from onboarding run for peregrine-60k (int4v2-experimental). We hit a very consistent rotary-phase drift that shows up as a one-token slip in the kvcache after ~36k tokens.
raj: repro command?
emma: ./ci/onboard_long.sh --model peregrine-60k --quant int4v2x --seq 37000 --seed 13 --batch 1
jyoti: log snippet pasted below. note the checksum delta and immediate token flip.
```
[kv] shard=0 write_pos=36012 expected_idx=36012 got_idx=36013
[rot] phase_accum=22618.472 -> reeval_phase=22618.469 delta=0.003
[token] emitted: "in" -> later emitted: "\n" at pos 36018
[perf] latency: 154ms -> 187ms around event
```
marc: interesting that reeval_phase != phase_accum by a small float; on quant path that delta can cause index rounding to shift by one. Is this seen on fp16?
emma: fp16 clean to 37k. int4v2x and int3 show problem. int8 is clean.
raj: can you try the renorm prototype? I pushed a tiny change to rotary: every RENORM_INTERVAL tokens we recompute sin/cos from pos instead of incrementally accumulating. It trades a small compute for stability. Flag is ROTARY_RENORM=5000.
emma: ran with ROTARY_RENORM=5000: failure moved to ~64k (ran extended) but repro still triggers eventually when combined with async kv compaction.
jyoti: typo — jyoti: also tried increasing RENORM to 1k and it eliminated the repro in a couple short trials but perf impact noticeable (~5-8% throughput loss).
marc: can we make renorm conditional: only run when cheap phase-check deviation detected? E.g., compute a lightweight checksum of sin/cos over a handful of indices; if checksum delta > threshold then do full renorm. That should catch drift but avoid periodic cost.
raj: good idea. I'll add DEBUG_ROPE_GUARD which computes a 16-lane dot-check every 1024 tokens. Cheap. If delta>1e-3 trigger renorm.
ops-bot: snapshot saved: s3://redwood-ci/peregrine/3099997777/snap.tar.gz (tags: int4v2x,renorm-test)
emma: on a related note, the int4v2x kernels pack accumulators differently (reduced accumulation precision), so rounding error builds up faster. We should consider a short-term mitigation fallback: for sequences > 16k, force the safer fp16 rotary path for phase computation while keeping rest of compute quantized. It's a small perf hit but keeps token correctness.
jyoti: I can prototype mixed-precision rotary: compute sin/cos in fp16->fp32 accumulators for updates, cast back to quant LUT writes. Should be cheap and address accumulation.
marc: also add an assertion in kvcache writer to verify write_pos==expected_idx and if not, dump small context and backtrace (but don't crash in perf runs).
raj: I'll open two PRs: one for DEBUG_ROPE_GUARD + conditional renorm, one for mixed-precision rotary fallback behind a runtime flag. Can we land the guard first (low perf cost)?
emma: yes please. Also schedule a matrix run for combinations: {quant: int4v2x,int3,int8,fp16} x {evict:async,sync} x {renorm:off,guard}. Bench-bot should run those overnight.
ops-bot: bench-bot scheduled matrix job 3099997777-matrix; results to s3://redwood-ci/peregrine/matrix/3099997777/
jyoti: final note: add telemetry when guard triggers (sampled) so we can correlate with models and kernels. Prefer sample rate 1% to avoid noise.
emma: agreed. Owners: raj (guard + PR), jyoti (mixed-precision prototype), marc (kvcache assertion + safe dump), emma (matrix runs + eval). Will reconvene after bench results. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
